events.title_en: Creation of Adam

events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 607 அக்டோபரில், பாபிலோனியரால் எருசலேம் வீழ்த்தப்பட்டு, தாவீதின் வம்சாவளியில் வந்த ராஜா சிங்காசனத்திலிருந்து நீக்கப்பட்டபோது அந்த 2,520 வருட காலப்பகுதி ஆரம்பமானது.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel’s Prophecy! (dp chap. 17 pp. 286-305)
sources.title_en: Identifying True Worshipers in the Time of the End
sources.quote_en: Seven times (2,520 years): October 607 B.C.E. to … October 1914 C.E.

sources.publication: What Does the Bible Really Teach? (bh p. 215-p. 218 par. 1)
sources.quote_en: The 2,520 years began in October 607 B.C.E., when Jerusalem fell to the Babylonians and the Davidic king was taken off his throne. The period ended in October 1914.

sources.publication: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1 (it-1 “Appointed Times of the Nations”)
sources.quote_en: This also confirms the start of “the appointed times of the nations” in the year of Jerusalem’s destruction, 607 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Ezekiel told that Jerusalem has been struck down
events.description_en: In Babylon, an escapee from Jerusalem reached Ezekiel and reported that the city had been struck down; Ezekiel was then free to speak again to the exiles.
events.description_ta: (33:17) இப்போது பொ.ச.மு. 607-ன் பத்தாவது மாதத்தின் ஐந்தாம் தேதி.

sources.quote_en: But now it is 607 B.C.E., the fifth day of the tenth month. An escapee arrives from Jerusalem

events.title_en: Nebuchadnezzar's dream of the immense image
events.description_en: In the second year of his reign as world ruler (counted from Jerusalem's destruction), Nebuchadnezzar had a terrifying dream of an immense image; Daniel revealed and interpreted it.
events.description_ta: நேபுகாத்நேச்சார் உலகை ஆட்சிபுரிந்த இரண்டாம் வருடத்தில் (பொ.ச.மு. 606/605) கடவுள் தந்த கனவால் அரண்டுபோனார்.

sources.quote_en: In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign as world ruler (606/605 B.C.E.), God sent him a terrifying dream.
In the second year of Nebuchadnezzar's kingship (evidently counting from the time of his conquest of Jerusalem in 607 B.C.E.)

events.title_en: Ezekiel's vision of a great temple
events.description_en: In the 14th year after Jerusalem's destruction, the priest-prophet Ezekiel was transported in vision to a high mountain and beheld a great temple of Jehovah.

sources.quote_en: In 593 B.C.E., in the 14th year after the destruction of Jerusalem ... Ezekiel ... beheld a great temple of Jehovah.

events.title_en: Ezekiel foretells Egypt given to Nebuchadnezzar
events.description_en: Ezekiel received a message that Egypt would be given to Nebuchadnezzar as wages for his campaign against Tyre; he inserted this later revelation into his book.
events.description_ta: இங்கே, பொ.ச.மு. 591-ல் தனக்கு வெளிப்படுத்தப்பட்ட சில தகவல்களை எசேக்கியேல் இடையில் சேர்க்கிறார்.

sources.quote_en: Ezekiel here inserts some information actually revealed to him later, in 591 B.C.E.
as foretold by the prophet Ezekiel evidently in the year 591 B.C.E.

series.label_en: Jehovah will give Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar as compensation for his service in wearing down Tyre

events.description_en: A fragmentary Babylonian text dated to Nebuchadnezzar's 37th year mentions a campaign against Egypt, possibly when Egypt was brought under Babylonian control as Ezekiel foretold.

sources.quote_en: One fragmentary Babylonian text, dated to Nebuchadnezzar's 37th year (588 B.C.E.), does, in fact, mention a campaign against Egypt.

events.title_en: Death of Nebuchadnezzar II
events.description_en: After a 43-year reign (624-582 B.C.E.) that included his 'seven times' of madness, Nebuchadnezzar died in October 582 B.C.E.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 582-ல் கர்வம்பிடித்த நேபுகாத்நேச்சாரின் உயிர்பிரிந்தது.

sources.quote_en: Nebuchadnezzar II died in October of 582 B.C.E. and was succeeded by Awil-Marduk (Evil-merodach).
Nebuchadnezzar ruled as king for 43 years (624-582 B.C.E.)

events.title_en: Cyrus begins his reign
events.description_en: Cyrus succeeded his father Cambyses I to the throne of Anshan in Persia about 560/559 B.C.E.; Diodorus places the start of his reign in Olympiad 55, year 1.
events.description_ta: சுமார் பொ.ச.மு. 560/559-ல் கோரேசு புகழின் பாதையில் காலடியெடுத்து வைத்தார்.

sources.quote_en: Diodorus (first century B.C.E.) places the start of Cyrus' reign in the first year of the 55th Olympiad, or 560/559 B.C.E.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 9
sources.quote_en: Cyrus' march to fame began about 560/559 B.C.E. when he succeeded his father Cambyses I to the throne of Anshan

events.title_en: Reign of Cyrus the Great
events.description_en: Cyrus, the Persian conqueror of Babylon, reigned from 560/559 B.C.E. and issued the decree that let the Jews return home; he died on a military campaign in 530 B.C.E.

sources.quote_en: places the start of Cyrus’ reign in the first year of the 55th Olympiad, or 560/559 B.C.E.
Cyrus is believed to have fallen in battle in 530 B.C.E.
Cyrus’ first year as king of Persia corresponded to Olympiad 55, year 1 (560/559 B.C.E.), while Cyrus’ last year is placed at Olympiad 62, year 2 (531/530 B.C.E.)

events.title_en: Nabonidus begins to rule Babylon
events.description_en: On the basis of cuneiform texts, Nabonidus is believed to have ruled Babylon some 17 years, from 556 to 539 B.C.E.
events.description_ta: நபோனிடஸ் தன் ஆட்சியை பொ.ச.மு. 556-ல் தொடங்கியதாக நம்பப்படுவதால் அவருடைய ஆட்சியின் மூன்றாம் வருஷமும் ‘பெல்ஷாத்சாரின் முதலாம் வருஷமும்’ பொ.ச.மு. 553 ஆக இருந்ததென தெரிகிறது.

sources.quote_en: On the basis of cuneiform texts he is believed to have ruled some 17 years (556-539 B.C.E.).
Since Nabonidus is believed to have begun his rule in 556 B.C.E.

events.title_en: First year of Belshazzar: Daniel's dream of four beasts
events.description_en: Belshazzar exercised royal authority from Nabonidus' third year on, evidently 553 B.C.E. In 'the first year of Belshazzar' Daniel had a dream and visions of four beasts, beginning the private visions of Daniel chapters 7 to 12.
events.description_ta: இவருடைய ஆட்சி பொ.ச.மு. 553-ல் தொடங்கியிருக்க வேண்டும்.

sources.quote_en: We return to 'the first year of Belshazzar,' whose reign evidently began in 553 B.C.E.
Belshazzar definitely exercised royal authority from Nabonidus' third year on

events.notes: Daniel 8 vision ('third year of Belshazzar') has no B.C.E. date stated on jw.org sources checked; not included.

events.title_en: Babylonian king Nabonidus conquers Edom
events.description_en: Babylon’s peace with Edom did not last: about the middle of the sixth century B.C.E., troops of the Babylonian king Nabonidus conquered Edom. Insight and “All Scripture Is Inspired” present this as a fulfillment of the prophecies of Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and Obadiah against Edom (Obadiah 7: those ‘in covenant with’ Edom would prevail against her).
events.description_ta: பாபிலோன் ஏதோமுடன் செய்த சமாதானம் நீண்ட காலம் நிலைக்கவில்லை. பொ.ச.மு. ஆறாம் நூற்றாண்டில், அரசன் நபோனிடஸின் பாபிலோனிய சேனைகள் ஏதோமை கைப்பற்றின.

sources.quote_en: Soon the time for Edom to drink deeply from the cup of Jehovah’s wrath arrived. (Jer 25:15-17, 21) This occurred about the middle of the sixth century B.C.E., under the Babylonian king Nabonidus.

sources.publication: “All Scripture Is Inspired of God and Beneficial” (si), Bible Book Number 31
sources.quote_en: Babylon’s peace with Edom did not last. During the sixth century B.C.E., Babylonian forces under King Nabonidus conquered Edom.

events.notes: No exact year is printed. Insight: “about the middle of the sixth century B.C.E.”; si (Tamil and English): “during the sixth century B.C.E.” Year 550 and sort_key -550 only place the event mid-century (Nabonidus began to rule in 556 B.C.E., b4-0019); do not display as a year.

events.description_en: After defeating Egypt's General Scopas at Paneas and taking Sidon, Antiochus the Great captured Jerusalem; Judea passed from the Ptolemaic king of the south to the Seleucid king of the north.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 198-ல், எருசலேமும் யூதாவும் எகிப்திய தென்றிசை ராஜாவிடமிருந்து சிரியா தேசத்து வடதிசை ராஜாவிடம் கைமாறின.

sources.quote_en: In 198 B.C.E. Antiochus the Great ... captured Jerusalem, and Judea became a dominion of the Seleucid Empire.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: In 198 B.C.E., Jerusalem and Judah passed from domination by the Egyptian king of the south to that of the Syrian king of the north.

series.label_en: Antiochus III takes Sidon and Jerusalem; Judea passes to the king of the north (198 B.C.E.)

events.title_en: Macedonia and Greece fall to the Romans
events.description_en: Macedonia and Greece, one of the four divisions of Alexander's empire, fell to the Romans.

sources.quote_en: Macedonia and Greece ... fell to the Romans in 197 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Antiochus III's daughter marries Ptolemy V
events.description_en: At the marriage of Antiochus III's daughter Cleopatra I to Ptolemy V, the Syrian king did not hand over the promised provinces.
events.description_ta: இருந்தாலும் பொ.ச.மு. 193-ல் திருமணம் நடந்தபோது, சிரியா தேசத்து ராஜா இந்த மாகாணங்களை ஐந்தாம் தாலமிக்கு தரவில்லை.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: At the marriage in 193 B.C.E., however, the Syrian king did not let these provinces go to Ptolemy V.

series.label_en: Cleopatra I given in marriage to Ptolemy V (193 B.C.E.)

events.title_en: War in Greece draws in Antiochus III
events.description_en: A war broke out in Greece, and Antiochus III was induced to come there, bringing him into conflict with Rome.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 192-ல் கிரீஸில் ஒரு யுத்தம் மூண்டது, இதனால் மூன்றாம் ஆண்டியோகஸ் கிரீஸுக்கு வர தூண்டப்பட்டார்.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: A war broke out in Greece in 192 B.C.E., and Antiochus III was induced to come to Greece.

series.label_en: Antiochus III turns to “the coastlands” (192 B.C.E.)

events.title_en: Antiochus III defeated by Rome at Magnesia
events.description_en: After losing the battle of Magnesia, Antiochus III had to give up everything in Greece, Asia Minor, and west of the Taurus Mountains.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: About a year after losing the battle of Magnesia in 190 B.C.E., he had to give up everything in Greece, Asia Minor

series.label_en: Rome defeats Antiochus III at Magnesia (190 B.C.E.)

events.title_en: Death of Antiochus III
events.description_en: Antiochus III died while trying to rob a temple at Elymais, Persia.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: Antiochus III died while trying to rob a temple at Elymaïs, Persia, in 187 B.C.E.

events.title_en: High priest Onias deposed by Antiochus Epiphanes
events.description_en: Antiochus IV Epiphanes deposed the Jewish high priest Onias; some Jewish commentators wrongly applied Daniel 9:26 to him.

sources.quote_en: a high priest, Onias, who was deposed by Antiochus Epiphanes in 175 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Antiochus IV humiliated by Rome; Macedonia defeated
events.description_en: Antiochus IV complied with Roman demands to withdraw from Egypt and returned to Syria; the same year Rome again defeated Macedonia.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 168-ல் அவர் சிரியாவுக்குத் திரும்புகிறார்.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 14
sources.quote_en: Humiliated, Antiochus IV complies with Roman demands and returns to Syria in 168 B.C.E.
Macedonia warred against the Romans but was again defeated in 168 B.C.E.

series.label_en: Antiochus IV bows to Rome’s demands (168 B.C.E.): the Syrian–Egyptian confrontation ends

events.title_en: Antiochus IV desecrates the temple
events.description_en: Seeking to Hellenize the Jews, Antiochus IV Epiphanes dedicated Jerusalem's temple to Zeus, built an altar on the great altar, and sacrificed swine there. This led to the Maccabean (Hasmonaean) revolt.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 167 டிசம்பரில், ஆலய பிரகாரத்தில் புறமத கடவுளுக்கு பலிபீடம் அமைக்கப்பட்டது.

sources.quote_en: On this occasion (Chislev 25, 168 B.C.E.) ... Antiochus sacrificed swine on the altar
This led to the Maccabean (or Hasmonaean) revolt.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: In December 167 B.C.E., a pagan altar was erected on top of the great altar

images.caption_en: Zeus. The Greek gods had human form and often were viewed as grossly immoral

conflicts.note: dp ch. 13 dates the pagan altar to December 167 B.C.E.; Insight 'Festival of Dedication', 'Jerusalem', 'Greece' and 'Temple' give 168 B.C.E. (Chislev 25). Insight value used as primary.

events.notes: display_ta/description_ta are from dp Tamil, which uses 167 (see conflicts).

events.title_en: Judas Maccabaeus rededicates the temple; Festival of Dedication
events.title_ta: கிரேக்க விக்கிரகாராதனையால் தீட்டுப்படுத்தப்பட்டபின் ஆலய மறுபிரதிஷ்டை; பிரதிஷ்டை பண்டிகை
events.description_en: After a three-year struggle, Judas Maccabaeus recaptured the city and temple, built a new altar, and rededicated it on Chislev 25, exactly three years after its profanation; the eight-day Festival of Dedication commemorates it.

sources.title_en: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
sources.quote_en: 165 B.C.E. Rededication of temple after desecration by Greek idolatry; Festival of Dedication
the rededication took place on Chislev 25, 165 B.C.E., exactly three years to the day

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: In 164 B.C.E., on the anniversary of the desecration, Judas Maccabaeus rededicated the temple

conflicts.note: dp ch. 13 dates the rededication to 164 B.C.E.; si and Insight give Chislev 25, 165 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Death of Antiochus IV
events.description_en: Antiochus IV died in 163 B.C.E.; later Seleucid kings did not occupy the position of 'the king of the north.'

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 14
sources.quote_en: even though other kings of the Seleucid dynasty rule Syria after Antiochus IV dies in 163 B.C.E.

series.label_en: Antiochus IV dies (163 B.C.E.); later Seleucid kings do not occupy the position of the king of the north

events.title_en: Maccabean Jews appeal to Rome
events.description_en: With the war against the Seleucids continuing, the Jews appealed to Rome for help, bringing Roman influence onto the Jerusalem scene.

sources.quote_en: The Jews appealed to Rome for help and thus a new power came on the Jerusalem scene in about 160 B.C.E.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: The Maccabees probably made a treaty with Rome in 161 B.C.E.

conflicts.note: dp ch. 13 says the Maccabees probably made a treaty with Rome in 161 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Septuagint translation completed
events.description_en: Translation of the entire Hebrew Scriptures into Greek was finally completed during the second century B.C.E., perhaps by 150 B.C.E.

sources.quote_en: translation of the entire Hebrew Scriptures had finally been completed during the second century B.C.E. and perhaps by 150 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Rome destroys Corinth; Achaia and Macedonia become provinces
events.description_en: After the Achaean League rebelled, Rome's armies destroyed Corinth and formed the province of Achaia; Macedonia also became a Roman province.
events.description_ta: காலப்போக்கில் மக்கெதோனியா ரோமைச் சார்ந்திருக்கலாயிற்று, இறுதியாக பொ.ச.மு. 146-ல் ரோமோடு இணைந்துவிட்டது.

sources.quote_en: Led by Corinth, the Achaean League rebelled in 146 B.C.E., and Rome's armies marched into southern Greece and destroyed Corinth.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: ended up as a Roman province in 146 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Simon Maccabaeus makes Jerusalem capital of a free region
events.description_en: Simon Maccabaeus made Jerusalem the capital of a region ostensibly free from subservience or taxation to Gentile nations.

sources.quote_en: About 142 B.C.E., Simon Maccabaeus was able to make Jerusalem the capital of a region ostensibly free

events.title_en: John Hyrcanus I forces circumcision on the Idumeans
events.description_en: According to Josephus, the Maccabean ruler John Hyrcanus I subjugated the Idumeans (Edomites) and forced circumcision on them; Herod's family were therefore nominally Jews.

sources.quote_en: the Idumeans had had circumcision forced upon them by the Maccabean ruler John Hyrcanus I in about 125 B.C.E.

series.label_en: The remaining Edomites were subjugated by the Jewish king John Hyrcanus I and forced to submit to circumcision
series.label_ta: யூத அரசனான முதலாம் ஜான் ஹிர்கனஸ் மீந்திருந்த ஏதோமியரைக் கீழ்ப்படுத்தி விருத்தசேதனம் செய்யும்படி அவர்களை வற்புறுத்தினார்.

events.title_en: Aristobulus I takes the title of king
events.description_en: Aristobulus I, Jerusalem's high priest and not of David's line, assumed the title of king, establishing a Maccabean kingdom.
events.description_ta: 38 மக்கபேயர்கள் பொ.ச.மு. 161-ல் ரோமோடு சமாதான ஒப்பந்தம் செய்து, பொ.ச.மு. 104-ல் ஒரு ராஜ்யத்தை ஏற்படுத்தியிருக்க வேண்டும்.

sources.quote_en: Aristobulus I, Jerusalem's high priest, even assumed the title of king in 104 B.C.E.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: established a kingdom in 104 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Pompey makes Syria a Roman province
events.description_en: Roman General Pompey made Syria a Roman province, ending the Seleucid dynasty.
events.description_ta: இறுதியாக பொ.ச.மு. 64-ல் சிரியா ரோம மாகாணமானது.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: his dynasty ruled until 64 B.C.E. when Roman General Gnaeus Pompey made Syria a Roman province.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 14

events.title_en: Pompey takes Jerusalem; Rome rules
events.title_ta: ரோம், ஆறாவது உலக வல்லரசு, எருசலேமை ஆளுகிறது
events.description_en: Called in to settle the quarrel between Aristobulus II and Hyrcanus, Roman forces under Pompey besieged Jerusalem for three months and took it; Rome, the sixth world power, now ruled Jerusalem.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 63-ல் ரோம தளபதியான நேயஸ் பாம்பி, எருசலேமை மூன்று மாதம் முற்றுகையிட்டுக் கைப்பற்றினார்.

sources.title_en: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
sources.quote_en: 63 B.C.E. Rome, sixth world power, rules Jerusalem
Under General Pompey, Roman forces besieged Jerusalem in 63 B.C.E.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: The Roman General Gnaeus Pompey took Jerusalem in 63 B.C.E. after a three-month siege.
Pompey, upon conquering Jerusalem in 63 B.C.E., took Jews to Rome as slaves.

images.caption_en: MAP: Jerusalem and Vicinity

conflicts.note: dp chs. 4, 9, 10 date Rome as world power 'from 30 B.C.E.' (fall of Ptolemaic Egypt); si says Rome rules Jerusalem from 63 B.C.E. Different reference points.

events.title_en: Julius Caesar invades Britannia
events.description_en: Roman General Julius Caesar invaded Britannia but failed to establish a permanent settlement.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 55-ல் ரோம தளபதி ஜூலியஸ் சீசர் பிரிட்டானியாமீது படையெடுத்தார், ஆனால் அவரால் ஒரு நிரந்தரமான குடியிருப்பை ஏற்படுத்த முடியவில்லை.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 9
sources.quote_en: In 55 B.C.E., Roman General Julius Caesar invaded Britannia but failed to establish a permanent settlement.

events.title_en: Lex Julia majestatis enacted
events.description_en: The law called lex Julia majestatis made it an offense to engage in any activity against the sovereign power of Rome, a background to the charges later brought against Jesus.

sources.quote_en: In 48 B.C.E., the law called lex Julia majestatis had made it an offense to engage in any activity against the sovereign power of Rome.

events.title_en: Herod made governor of Galilee
events.description_en: Antipater II appointed his son Herod governor of Galilee, where Herod distinguished himself by ridding the territory of robber bands.

sources.quote_en: the time Herod received his appointment as governor of Galilee (which is generally dated 47 B.C.E.)

events.title_en: Julius Caesar appointed dictator
events.description_en: Gaius Julius Caesar was appointed dictator of Rome for ten years.

sources.quote_en: In 46 B.C.E., Gaius Julius Caesar was appointed dictator of Rome for ten years

events.title_en: Julius Caesar assassinated
events.description_en: Julius Caesar was murdered by conspirators; his great-nephew Octavian was then only 18.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 44-ல் ஜூலியஸ் சீசர் கொலைசெய்யப்பட்ட போது, அவரது சகோதரியின் பேரனான கயஸ் ஆக்டேவியனுக்கு 18 வயதுதான்.

sources.quote_en: but he was murdered in 44 B.C.E.
murdered by conspirators in 44 B.C.E.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 14
sources.quote_en: In 44 B.C.E. when Julius Caesar was assassinated, his sister's grandson Gaius Octavian was only 18 years of age.

events.title_en: Herod appointed king of Judea by the Roman Senate
events.description_en: On Mark Antony's recommendation, the Roman senate appointed the Edomite Herod king of greater Judea, though he could not establish himself in Jerusalem until about three years later.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 39-ல், ரோம பேரவை ஏதோமியரான ஏரோதை யூதேயாவின் ராஜாவாக்கியது.

sources.quote_en: about 39 B.C.E., was made king of greater Judea by appointment of the Roman senate

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: In 39 B.C.E., the Roman Senate appointed Herod—an Edomite—to be king of Judea.

images.caption_en: Ruins of multileveled palace built by Herod the Great atop Masada

conflicts.note: Insight 'Herod' notes Josephus' method would place the appointment in 40 B.C.E., while Appianos' data place it in 39 B.C.E.

endpoint_of.span_title: Reign of Herod the Great over Judea

events.title_en: Reign of Herod the Great over Judea
events.description_en: The Roman Senate made the Edomite Herod king of Judea about 39 B.C.E.; three years later he took Jerusalem. He rebuilt the temple and ordered the killing of the boys of Bethlehem, and he likely died in 1 B.C.E.

sources.publication: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1 (it-1 “Herod” No. 1 ¶1-No. 6 ¶2)
sources.quote_en: about 39 B.C.E., was made king of greater Judea by appointment of the Roman senate; but he was not able to establish himself as de facto king until three years later

sources.publication: Insight on the Scriptures, Vol. 1 (it-1 “Herod” No. 1 ¶1-No. 6 ¶2)
sources.quote_en: The available evidence indicates that Herod died likely in the year 1 B.C.E.

conflicts.note: Insight “Jerusalem” says Herod “did not get control of Jerusalem until 37 or 36 B.C.E., from which date his rule effectively began.”

events.title_en: Herod takes Jerusalem by storm
events.title_ta: ஏரோது (ரோம் நியமித்த அரசன்) மூர்க்கத் தாக்குதலால் எருசலேமைக் கைப்பற்றுகிறார்
events.description_en: Herod, appointed king by Rome, took Jerusalem and deposed Antigonus, ending Maccabean rule; his rule effectively began from this date.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 37-ல் எருசலேமை இவர் கைப்பற்றவே, மக்கபேயர்களின் ஆட்சி முடிவுக்கு வந்தது.

sources.title_en: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
sources.quote_en: c. 37 B.C.E. Herod (appointed king by Rome) takes Jerusalem by storm

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 13
sources.quote_en: Ending the Maccabean rule, he took Jerusalem in 37 B.C.E.
He did not get control of Jerusalem until 37 or 36 B.C.E., from which date his rule effectively began.

conflicts.note: Insight 'Herod' notes Josephus also says it was 27 years after Pompey's capture (63), which would make it 36 B.C.E.; Insight 'Jerusalem' says '37 or 36'.

events.title_en: Octavian defeats Antony and Cleopatra at Actium
events.description_en: At the battle of Actium, Octavian defeated the combined forces of Cleopatra VII and Mark Antony and emerged as the undisputed ruler of the Roman Empire.
events.description_ta: (தானியேல் 11:14) பொ.ச.மு. 31-ல், ஆக்டியம் யுத்தத்தின்போது, தாலமிய வம்சத்தின் கடைசி ராணியான ஏழாம் க்ளியோபாட்ரா, அவளது ரோம காதலன் மார்க் ஆன்டனி ஆகிய இருவரது ஒன்றிணைந்த படைகளையும் ரோம அரசரான ஆக்டேவியன் வீழ்த்தினார்.

sources.quote_en: In September, 31 B.C.E. ... Octavius emerged the undisputed ruler of the Roman Empire.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 14
sources.quote_en: During the battle of Actium, in 31 B.C.E., Roman ruler Octavian defeats the combined forces of the last Ptolemaic queen

series.label_en: Actium (31 B.C.E.): Octavian defeats Cleopatra VII and Mark Antony

events.title_en: Reign of Augustus (Octavian), Roman emperor
events.description_en: Octavian became undisputed ruler of the Roman Empire after Actium in 31 B.C.E. and received the title Augustus in 27 B.C.E.; his registration decree brought Jesus’ birth at Bethlehem. He died in 14 C.E.

sources.quote_en: Augustus … 31 B.C.E.–14 C.E.
In September, 31 B.C.E., 13 years after the assassination of his great-uncle Julius Caesar, Octavius emerged the undisputed ruler of the Roman Empire.
Augustus died August 17, 14 C.E. (August 19, Julian calendar)

conflicts.note: Insight “Chronology” counts “Augustus’ rule ran from 27 B.C.E. to 14 C.E.” (from his title Augustus); the Insight “Caesar” table starts it in 31 B.C.E.

events.title_en: Ptolemaic Egypt falls to Rome
events.description_en: The Ptolemaic dynasty, last of the four Hellenistic kingdoms, fell to Rome; by 30 B.C.E. Rome had supremacy over Syria and Egypt and emerged as the world power of Bible prophecy.
events.description_ta: தாலமியின் ராஜ வம்சம், பொ.ச.மு. 30-ல் எகிப்தை ரோம் கைப்பற்றியது வரை ஆட்சியில் இருந்தது.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 9
sources.quote_en: The Ptolemaic dynasty continued to rule in Egypt until it fell to Rome in 30 B.C.E.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 14
sources.quote_en: By the year 30 B.C.E., Rome has supremacy over both Syria and Egypt.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 4
sources.title_en: The Rise and Fall of an Immense Image

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel's Prophecy! (dp) ch. 10
sources.title_en: Who Can Stand Against the Prince of Princes?
sources.title_ta: அதிபதிகளுக்கெல்லாம் அதிபதிக்கு முன்பாக நிற்க துணிந்தவர் யார்?

series.label_en: Egypt becomes a Roman province and no longer plays the role of the king of the south (30 B.C.E.)
Ptolemaic Egypt falls to Rome (30 B.C.E.)
30 B.C.E. Ptolemaic Egypt, the last Hellenistic kingdom, falls to Rome

events.title_en: Rome, sixth world power
events.description_en: By 30 B.C.E. Rome had taken over all the Hellenistic kingdoms and become the sixth world power; it executed Jesus, persecuted his disciples, and destroyed Jerusalem in 70 C.E.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச.மு. 30-ம் ஆண்டிற்குள், ரோம் எல்லா கிரேக்க ராஜ்யங்களையும் வென்று, பைபிள் சரித்திரத்தின் ஆறாம் உலக வல்லரசானது.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel’s Prophecy! (dp chap. 10 pp. 164-179)
sources.title_en: Who Can Stand Against the Prince of Princes?
sources.title_ta: அதிபதிகளுக்கெல்லாம் அதிபதிக்கு முன்பாக நிற்க துணிந்தவர் யார்?
sources.quote_en: And by the year 30 B.C.E., Rome took over all the Hellenistic kingdoms, making itself the sixth world power of Bible prophecy.

sources.publication: Pay Attention to Daniel’s Prophecy! (dp chap. 4 pp. 46-67)
sources.title_en: The Rise and Fall of an Immense Image

events.title_en: Augustus sends out “an exactor” by ordering a registration
events.description_en: In 2 B.C.E. Augustus, the king of the north of Daniel 11:20, ordered a registration, or census, that included the province of Judea. Because of this decree Joseph and Mary traveled to Bethlehem, where Jesus was born.

events.title_en: Death of Herod the Great
events.description_en: Bible chronology, astronomical data, and historical records point to 1 B.C.E. (or possibly early 1 C.E.) for Herod's death, shortly after his decree to kill Bethlehem's babes; a total lunar eclipse occurred on January 8, 1 B.C.E.

sources.quote_en: The available evidence indicates that Herod died likely in the year 1 B.C.E.
there is evidence pointing to the year 1 B.C.E. as the likely time of his death.
Herod died, evidently in the year 1 B.C.E.

conflicts.note: Insight notes some chronologers hold 5 or 4 B.C.E. based on the partial eclipse of March 11, 4 B.C.E.; jw.org favors 1 B.C.E.

events.notes: Outside strict 3 B.C.E. scope; included per orchestrator instruction.

events.title_en: Jesus baptized and anointed; Jehovah declares him his Son and approves him

events.title_en: Jesus’ earthly ministry
events.description_en: From his baptism and anointing in the fall of 29 C.E. until his death on Nisan 14, 33 C.E., Jesus preached the Kingdom for three and a half years, a period including four Passovers.

events.description_ta: அகாயா நாட்டின் ஆளுநராக கல்லியோனின் பதவி காலம் பொ.ச. 51-⁠ன் கோடைக்காலத்திலிருந்து பொ.ச. 52-⁠ன் கோடைகாலம் வரையில் நீடித்ததாக தோன்றுகிறது.

sources.quote_en: therefore appears to have run from the summer of 51 C.E. to the summer of 52 C.E., though some scholars favor 52-53 C.E.

sources.title_en: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
sources.quote_en: Gallio’s year as proconsul of Achaia appears to have run from the summer of 51 C.E. to the summer of 52 C.E.

images.caption_en: Portion of an inscription bearing the name Gallio

events.notes: Insight notes that some (non-Witness) scholars favor 52-53 C.E.; not a conflict between jw.org sources.

events.title_en: Paul brought before Gallio’s judgment seat and released
events.description_en: While Gallio was proconsul, the Jews of Corinth brought Paul before the judgment seat, but Gallio dismissed the case; Paul stayed “quite some days longer” and then sailed for Syria in the spring of 52.
events.description_ta: ‘கல்லியோன் அகாயா நாட்டு அதிபதியாக [ஆளுநராக] இருக்கையில் யூதர் ஏகமனதாக பவுலுக்கு விரோதமாய் எழும்பி அவரை நியாயாசனத்தின்முன் கொண்டுபோனார்கள்.’

sources.title_en: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
sources.quote_en: All of this seems to confirm the spring of 52 C.E. as the conclusion of Paul’s 18-month stay in Corinth.

images.caption_en: Gallio dismissing Paul’s case (Acts 18:16)

events.title_en: Felix becomes procurator of Judea
events.description_en: Most scholars date the start of Antonius Felix’s sole procuratorship of Judea to 52 C.E.; Tacitus indicates he served earlier jointly with Cumanus.

sources.quote_en: most scholars say that Felix began to serve as procurator in 52 C.E.

events.title_en: Apollos taught by Aquila and Priscilla in Ephesus
events.description_en: The eloquent Alexandrian Jew Apollos, who knew only John’s baptism, was taught the way of God more accurately by Aquila and Priscilla in Ephesus and went on to help the brothers in Achaia.

sources.publication: NWT Study Edition, Acts study notes
sources.quote_en: The events involving Apollos, described here, happened about the year 52 C.E.

events.title_en: Paul returns to Syrian Antioch, ending his second journey
events.description_en: After sailing from Corinth via Ephesus to Caesarea and greeting the congregation, apparently in Jerusalem, Paul arrived back at Syrian Antioch, probably in the summer of 52 C.E.
events.description_ta: சீரியாவிலுள்ள அந்தியோகியாவுக்கே பெரும்பாலும் பொ.ச. 52-⁠ன் கோடைகாலத்தில் வந்து சேர்ந்தார்.

sources.title_en: Study Number 3—Measuring Events in the Stream of Time
sources.quote_en: he arrived back at his home base of Syrian Antioch, probably in the summer of 52 C.E.

events.title_en: Paul’s third missionary journey
events.description_en: Paul set out again from Syrian Antioch, labored some three years in Ephesus, then traveled through Macedonia to Greece and back, arriving in Jerusalem by Pentecost 56 C.E.
events.description_ta: பவுலின் மூன்றாவது மிஷனரி பயணம், ஏ. பொ.ச. 52-56.

On his third missionary journey (c. 52-56 C.E.), Paul revisited Ephesus and labored there for some three years.

events.title_en: Nero becomes Roman emperor
events.description_en: After Claudius died in 54 C.E., Nero, his adopted son, took the throne at about 17; all references to Caesar in Acts chapters 25 to 28 apply to him.

sources.publication: NWT Study Edition, Acts study notes
sources.quote_en: The Roman emperor at this time was Nero. His rule began in 54 C.E.
Nero, who ruled from 54 to 68 C.E.

events.title_en: Reign of Nero, Roman emperor
events.description_en: Nero was the Caesar to whom Paul appealed; after the great fire of Rome in 64 C.E. he began strong official persecution of Christians. He committed suicide in 68 C.E.

sources.quote_en: Nero … 54-68 C.E.

events.description_en: Paul apparently left Ephesus after the festival of Pentecost in 55 C.E., traveling through Macedonia to Corinth, Greece, where he spent three winter months.

events.title_en: Paul appeals to Caesar before Festus
events.description_en: On trial before Festus in Caesarea, Paul refused a transfer of the trial to Jerusalem and appealed to Caesar (Nero); Festus admitted the appeal after consulting his counselors.

sources.quote_en: It was to Nero that Paul referred when on trial in Caesarea before Festus, evidently about 58 C.E.

events.description_en: During a courtesy visit to Festus with his sister Bernice, King Herod Agrippa II heard Paul’s defense and concluded that Paul could have been released had he not appealed to Caesar.

events.title_en: Shipwreck on Malta; Paul winters there
events.description_en: Driven by a storm, the ship carrying Paul ran aground and broke up off Malta; all 276 aboard reached land safely, and they wintered on the island before sailing on to Italy.
events.description_ta: பவுல் பயணம்செய்த கப்பல், சேதத்திற்கு உள்ளான பின்னும் மெலித்தாவில் குளிர்காலத்தைக் கழித்த பின்பும் அந்தப் பயணம் சுமார் பொ.ச. 59-⁠ல் முடிவுற்றது.

events.title_en: Paul arrives at Puteoli and Rome
events.description_en: Sailing from Malta via Rhegium, Paul landed at Puteoli about 59 C.E. and traveled the Appian Way to Rome, where brothers met him at the Marketplace of Appius and Three Taverns.

events.title_en: Paul’s first imprisonment (house arrest) in Rome
events.title_ta: ரோமில் முதல் முறையாக பவுல் சிறையில் அடைக்கப்படுகிறார்
events.description_en: For two years Paul remained under guard in his own rented house in Rome, preaching the Kingdom to all who came to him; during this time he wrote several letters.
events.description_ta: பவுல் ரோமில் இரண்டு ஆண்டு காலம், அல்லது பொ.ச. 61 வரை, சிறைக்காவலில் பிரசங்கித்துக்கொண்டும் கற்பித்துக்கொண்டும் இருந்தாரென பதிவு காட்டுகிறது.

events.title_en: James, Jesus' brother and writer of James, stoned (per Josephus)
events.description_en: According to the historian Josephus, cited in 'All Scripture Is Inspired', James the brother of Jesus was stoned at the instigation of High Priest Ananus after the death of Governor Festus, about 62 C.E.
events.description_ta: சதுசேயனும் பிரதான ஆசாரியனுமாகிய அனானஸேதான் (அனனியாஸ்) யாக்கோபின் மரணத்துக்கு காரணம் என்பதாகவும், அவர் கல்லெறிந்து கொல்லப்பட்டார் என்பதாகவும் சரித்திராசிரியன் ஜொஸிஃபஸ் சொல்கிறார். இது ஏறக்குறைய பொ.ச. 62-ல் ரோம அதிபதி பெஸ்துவின் மரணத்திற்குப் பின், அல்பினஸ் பதவி ஏற்பதற்கு முன் நடந்திருக்க வேண்டும்.

sources.quote_en: Josephus tells us it was High Priest Ananus (Ananias), a Sadducee, who was responsible for the death of James by stoning.

events.title_en: Great fire ravages Rome
events.description_en: A great fire swept through Rome in July 64 C.E., causing extensive damage in 10 of the city’s 14 regions; Nero blamed the Christians.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச. 64 ஜூலையில் ரோம் நகரமே தீப்பற்றி எரிந்து பெரிய நாசத்தை ஏற்படுத்தியது. அந்த நகரத்தின் 14 பிராந்தியங்களில் 10-⁠ல் மிகுதியான சேதம் ஏற்பட்டிருந்தது.

events.description_en: From the middle of the second century, professed Christians trained in Greek philosophy began expressing their faith in its terms. Apostate Christians of that century took on pagan Roman trappings and were imbued with Greek philosophy.

events.title_en: Canon of the Christian Greek Scriptures recognized as closed
events.description_en: By the end of the second century there was no question that the canon of the Christian Greek Scriptures was closed; writers such as Irenaeus, Clement of Alexandria, and Tertullian treated those writings as having authority equal to the Hebrew Scriptures. The Christian Greek Scriptures had also been translated into Latin by then.

events.title_en: Symmachus' Greek version of the Hebrew Scriptures

events.description_en: About 245 C.E., Origen of Alexandria completed the Hexapla, a six-column edition of the Hebrew Scriptures including the Hebrew text, a Greek transliteration, and Greek versions. Its Septuagint column contained the divine name in Hebrew characters.

events.title_en: Bishop of Rome first called "Pope"
events.description_en: The title "pope" was not used during the first two centuries. The first Bishop of Rome to be called "Pope" seems to have been Callistus in the third century.

events.title_en: Clergy-laity distinction becomes prominent (death of Cyprian)
events.description_en: Cyprian, "bishop" of Carthage, strongly advocated the authority of bishops as a group separate from presbyters, deacons, and laity. From his time (he died about 258 C.E.) the distinction between clergy and laity became prominent, and from the third century the term clerus was applied almost exclusively to the ministry.

events.title_en: Diocletian orders churches razed and copies of the Scriptures burned
events.description_en: On February 23, 303 C.E., Emperor Diocletian reportedly watched soldiers burn copies of the Scriptures in a church; the next day he decreed that Bibles throughout the empire be publicly burned and Christian meeting places razed. The persecution continued for a decade, yet copies survived.

sources.title_ta: சிரிலும் மெத்தோடியஸும் எழுத்துக்களை உருவாக்கிய பைபிள் மொழிபெயர்ப்பாளர்கள்
sources.quote_en: However, in 870 C.E., the Frankish bishop Hermanrich, with the help of Prince Svatopluk of Nitra, arrested Methodius.

events.title_en: Synod at Constantinople condemns the pope over the filioque clause
events.description_en: The Western church added filioque ("and from the Son") to the Nicene Creed. In 876 a synod at Constantinople condemned the pope for his political activities and for not correcting the filioque "heresy."
events.description_ta: ஆறாம் நூற்றாண்டில் செய்யப்பட்ட இந்தத் திருத்தத்தால் ஒரு பிளவு ஏற்பட்டது; “கான்ஸ்டான்டிநோப்பிளில் 876-ல் கூடிய [பிஷப்புகளின்] பேரவை போப்பை அவருடைய அரசியல் நடவடிக்கைகளுக்காகவும் மதபேதத்திற்கு வழிநடத்திய ஃபிலியோக்யு என்ற வார்த்தையை திருத்த தவறியதற்காகவும் கண்டனம் செய்தது.

sources.quote_en: The end result of this sixth-century emendation was a rift when “in 876 a synod [of bishops] at Constantinople condemned the pope both for his political activities and because he did not correct the heresy of the ...

events.title_en: Methodius dies; disciples expelled from Moravia
events.title_ta: பொ.ச. 885-⁠ல் மெத்தோடியஸின் மரணத்திற்குப்பின், ஃப்ரான்கிய எதிரிகள் இவருடைய சீஷர்களை மொராவியாவிலிருந்து வெளியேற்றினர்
events.description_en: After Methodius died in 885 C.E., his disciples were expelled from Moravia and took refuge in Bohemia, southern Poland, and Bulgaria, spreading the Slavonic written language.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச. 885-⁠ல் மெத்தோடியஸின் மரணத்திற்குப்பின், ஃப்ரான்கிய எதிரிகள் இவருடைய சீஷர்களை மொராவியாவிலிருந்து வெளியேற்றினர்.

sources.title_en: Cyril and Methodius—Bible Translators Who Invented an Alphabet
sources.title_ta: சிரிலும் மெத்தோடியஸும் எழுத்துக்களை உருவாக்கிய பைபிள் மொழிபெயர்ப்பாளர்கள்
sources.quote_en: After Methodius died in 885 C.E., his disciples were expelled from Moravia by their Frankish opponents.

events.title_en: Cairo Karaite Codex of the Prophets completed by Moses ben Asher
events.description_en: The Cairo Karaite Codex of the Prophets, with Masora and vocalization, was completed in about 895 C.E. by the noted Masorete Moses ben Asher of Tiberias.

sources.quote_en: It contains the Masora and vocalization, and its colophon indicates that it was completed in about 895 C.E. by the noted Masorete Moses ben Asher of Tiberias.

sources.title_en: Study Number 5—The Hebrew Text of the Holy Scriptures
sources.quote_en: Date 895 C.E.

events.title_en: Petersburg Codex of the Latter Prophets
events.description_en: The Petersburg Codex of the Latter Prophets, of 916 C.E., exhibits the Babylonian system of vowel pointing and is preserved in St. Petersburg.
events.description_ta: பொ.ச. 916-⁠ல் எழுதப்பட்ட தீர்க்கதரிசிகளின் பீட்டர்ஸ்பர்க் கோடக்ஸில், இந்த பாபிலோனிய குறியீட்டு முறையை பயன்படுத்தியிருக்கின்றனர்; இந்த கையெழுத்துப்பிரதி, ரஷ்யாவின் லெனின்கிராட் பொது நூல் நிலையத்தில் பாதுகாக்கப்படுகிறது.

sources.quote_en: Another significant manuscript (of 916 C.E.) is the Petersburg Codex of the Latter Prophets.

sources.title_en: Study Number 5—The Hebrew Text of the Holy Scriptures
sources.quote_en: A manuscript exhibiting the Babylonian pointing is the Petersburg Codex of the Prophets, of 916 C.E., preserved in the Leningrad Public Library, U.S.S.R. This codex contains Isaiah, Jeremiah, Ezekiel, and the ...

events.title_en: Aleppo Codex pointed and annotated by Aaron ben Asher
events.description_en: The Aleppo Codex, an important Hebrew Masoretic manuscript, was corrected, punctuated, and furnished with the Masora about 930 C.E. by Aaron ben Asher. Until 1947 it contained the entire Hebrew Scriptures.
events.description_ta: சுமார் கி.பி. 930-ஐச் சேர்ந்த முக்கியமான எபிரெய மசோரெட்டிக் கையெழுத்துப் பிரதியான அலெப்போ கோடெக்சில் இருக்கும் ஏசாயா 40-வது அதிகாரம்

sources.title_en: A3 How the Bible Came to Us
sources.quote_en: Chapter 40 of Isaiah’s book in the Aleppo Codex, an important Hebrew Masoretic manuscript from about 930 C.E.
Its original consonantal text was corrected, punctuated, and furnished with the Masora about 930 C.E. by Aaron ben Asher, son of Moses ben Asher.

sources.title_en: Study Number 5—The Hebrew Text of the Holy Scriptures
sources.quote_en: Date 930 C.E.
Portion of the Aleppo Codex.

images.caption_en: Chapter 40 of Isaiah's book in the Aleppo Codex, an important Hebrew Masoretic manuscript from about 930 C.E.
Portion of the Aleppo Codex with Masoretic marginal note

events.title_en: Leningrad Codex copied — oldest complete Masoretic manuscript
events.description_en: The Leningrad Manuscript No. B 19A, the oldest dated manuscript of the complete Hebrew Scriptures, was copied in 1008 C.E. It is the base text of modern critical editions used for the New World Translation.
events.description_ta: இது கி.பி. 1008/1009-ஆம் வருஷத்தைச் சேர்ந்தது.

sources.title_en: A3 How the Bible Came to Us
sources.quote_en: The oldest complete Masoretic manuscript is the Leningrad Codex, which dates from 1008/1009 C.E. However, in the middle of the 20th century, some 220 Biblical manuscripts or fragments were discovered among the Dead ...
It was copied in 1008 C.E. “from the corrected books prepared and annotated by Aaron ben Moses ben Asher the teacher.”

sources.title_en: Study Number 5—The Hebrew Text of the Holy Scriptures
sources.quote_en: Date 1008 C.E.

conflicts.note: NWT Study Edition App. A3 dates the Leningrad Codex 1008/1009 C.E.; Insight says copied in 1008 C.E.

events.title_en: Final break between Eastern and Western churches
events.description_en: In 1054 the pope's representative excommunicated the patriarch of Constantinople, who cursed the pope in return. The split led to the Eastern Orthodox Churches and the division between Roman Catholicism and Eastern Orthodoxy.
events.description_ta: (மனிதனின் மதங்கள்) கான்ஸ்டான்டிநோப்பிளில் இருந்த ஒரு தலைமை குருவை 1054-ஆம் ஆண்டில் போப்பின் பிரதிநிதி திருச்சபையிலிருந்து நீக்கினார், அவரோ பதிலுக்கு போப்பை சபித்தார்.

sources.quote_en: (Man’s Religions) In the year 1054, the pope’s representative excommunicated the patriarch of Constantinople, who in return put a curse on the pope.

sources.title_en: They Tried to Keep God’s Word From the Masses
sources.quote_en: Increasing tensions between the Western and Eastern branches of Christendom led to the division between Roman Catholicism and Eastern Orthodoxy in 1054.
In 1054 it lost control of the Eastern Church.

events.title_en: Pope Gregory VII bans the vernacular (Slavonic) Scriptures
events.description_en: In 1079, replying to Duke Vratislaus of Bohemia, Pope Gregory VII refused permission to use Slavonic in church services, writing that it pleased God that Scripture be "a secret in certain places." It was the first of many medieval edicts against vernacular versions.
events.description_ta: 1079-ல், ஏழாவது போப் க்ரிகரி, தாய் மொழியில் பைபிளை தயாரிப்பதையும் சிலசமயங்களில் அவற்றை வைத்திருப்பதையும்கூட தடைசெய்யும் சர்ச்சின் இடைக்கால உத்தரவுகள் பலவற்றில் முதலாவதானதைப் பிறப்பித்தார்.

sources.title_en: Part One—How the Bible Came to Us
sources.quote_en: In 1079, Pope Gregory VII issued the first of many medieval church edicts banning the production and sometimes even the possession of vernacular versions.

sources.title_en: Part One—How the Bible Came to Us
sources.quote_en: Edict against vernacular Bible 1079 C.E.

sources.title_en: They Tried to Keep God’s Word From the Masses
sources.quote_en: Thus, in response to the request made in 1079 by Vratislaus, duke of Bohemia, seeking permission to use Slavonic in local church services, Pope Gregory VII wrote: “We cannot in any way grant this petition.”

events.title_en: Pope Urban II launches the Crusade appeal at Clermont
events.title_ta: நவம்பர் 27, 1095-ல் பிரான்ஸிலுள்ள கிளர்மான்டில் நடைபெற்ற ஒரு அவைக்கு முன்பாக அர்பன் தன்னுடைய அழைப்பாணையை விடுத்தார்
events.description_en: On November 27, 1095, before a council at Clermont, France, Pope Urban II appealed for a war against the Muslims, promising remission of sins to those who died on the way or in battle.
events.description_ta: நவம்பர் 27, 1095-ல் பிரான்ஸிலுள்ள கிளர்மான்டில் நடைபெற்ற ஒரு அவைக்கு முன்பாக அர்பன் தன்னுடைய அழைப்பாணையை விடுத்தார்.

sources.quote_en: On November 27, 1095, before a council at Clermont, France, Urban launched his appeal.

events.title_en: First Crusade sets out
events.title_ta: ஏறக்குறைய தொளாயிரம் ஆண்டுகளுக்கு முன்பு, 1096-ல், முதலாவது சிலுவைப் போர் ஆரம்பிக்கும் தறுவாயில் இருந்தது
events.description_en: In 1096 the First Crusade began, the first of eight major Crusades accompanied by massacres committed in the name of God and Christ. A mob led by Peter the Hermit left Cologne on April 20, 1096; the official departure date was August 15, 1096.
events.description_ta: ஏறக்குறைய தொளாயிரம் ஆண்டுகளுக்கு முன்பு, 1096-ல், முதலாவது சிலுவைப் போர் ஆரம்பிக்கும் தறுவாயில் இருந்தது.

sources.quote_en: SOME nine hundred years ago, in 1096, the First Crusade was about to begin.
Once the departure date, August 15, 1096, was fixed, the pope ensured the support of lay lords, to whom military operations were entrusted.

events.title_en: The First Crusade
events.description_en: Crusader armies set out in 1096 and, after a long march, took Jerusalem on July 15, 1099, with a massacre of its inhabitants.
events.description_ta: ஜூலை 15, 1099-ல் ஜெரூசலம் சிலுவைப் போர் வீரர்களிடம் வீழ்ச்சியடைந்தது.

sources.quote_en: In the meantime, during the summer of 1096, trained armies set out.
On July 15, 1099, Jerusalem fell to the crusaders.

events.title_en: The Crusades
events.description_en: Launched by Pope Urban II, the Crusades were two centuries of so-called holy wars against the Muslims for control of Jerusalem, from the First Crusade in 1096 to the fall of Acre, the last crusader stronghold, in 1291.
events.description_ta: 1291-ல் சிலுவைப் போர் வீரர்களின் கடைசி அரணான பட்டணமாகிய ஏக்கர் முஸ்லிம்களிடம் வீழ்ச்சியடைந்தது.

sources.quote_en: SOME nine hundred years ago, in 1096, the First Crusade was about to begin.
In 1291 the city of Acre, the last crusader stronghold, fell to the Muslims.
During two centuries of conflict, economic and political interests had dominated religious questions.

events.title_en: Jerusalem falls to the crusaders amid massacre
events.title_ta: ஜூலை 15, 1099-ல் ஜெரூசலம் சிலுவைப் போர் வீரர்களிடம் வீழ்ச்சியடைந்தது
events.description_en: On July 15, 1099, Jerusalem fell to the crusaders, who slaughtered its inhabitants and tried to justify the violence in the name of religion.
events.description_ta: ஜூலை 15, 1099-ல் ஜெரூசலம் சிலுவைப் போர் வீரர்களிடம் வீழ்ச்சியடைந்தது.

sources.quote_en: On July 15, 1099, Jerusalem fell to the crusaders.

events.title_en: Vaudès (Peter Waldo) starts the Waldensian preaching movement
events.title_ta: அந்த இயக்கம் சுமார் 1170-⁠ம் வருடத்தில் தொடங்கியதாக அநேக வரலாற்றாசிரியர்கள் ஒத்துக்கொள்கின்றனர்
events.description_en: About 1170, Vaudès, a wealthy merchant of Lyons, gave up his riches to preach the Gospel and had parts of the Bible translated into the language of southern France. His followers, the Waldenses, rejected purgatory, indulgences, and other Catholic teachings.
events.description_ta: அந்த இயக்கம் சுமார் 1170-⁠ம் வருடத்தில் தொடங்கியதாக அநேக வரலாற்றாசிரியர்கள் ஒத்துக்கொள்கின்றனர்.

sources.quote_en: Most historians agree that the movement had its start about the year 1170.
In the 12th century, Peter Waldo, from Lyons, France, “engaged some scholars to translate the Bible into the langue d’oc [a regional language] of south France.

events.title_en: Vaudès seeks papal authorization to preach; lay preaching forbidden
events.description_en: In 1179 Vaudès sought authorization to preach from Pope Alexander III, which was granted only on condition of local priests' approval. The archbishop of Lyons then forbade lay preaching; Vaudès replied by quoting Acts 5:29.
events.description_ta: வால்டென்ஸ்களை ஒன்றும் அறியாதவர்களும் படிப்பறிவற்றவர்களுமாக மதகுருமார் கருதினர்; ஆனால் 1179-⁠ல், பிரசங்கிப்பதற்கு அதிகாரப்பூர்வமான அனுமதியளிக்கும்படி போப் மூன்றாம் அலெக்ஸாண்டரிடம் வாடீ கேட்டுக்கொண்டார்.

sources.quote_en: The clergy considered the Waldenses ignorant and illiterate, but in 1179, Vaudès sought official authorization for his preaching from Pope Alexander III.

events.title_en: Pope Lucius III establishes the Inquisition at Verona
events.title_ta: கவுன்சில் ஆஃப் வெரோனாவில் மூன்றாம் போப் லூஸியஸ் என்பவர் இந்த ஒடுக்குமுறை விசாரணை மன்றத்தை 1184-ல் நிறுவினார்
events.description_en: Pope Lucius III established the Inquisition at the Council of Verona in 1184; later popes perfected its procedures, and in the 13th century Gregory IX set up inquisitorial tribunals across Europe.
events.description_ta: கவுன்சில் ஆஃப் வெரோனாவில் மூன்றாம் போப் லூஸியஸ் என்பவர் இந்த ஒடுக்குமுறை விசாரணை மன்றத்தை 1184-ல் நிறுவினார்.

sources.title_en: The Trial and Execution of a “Heretic”
sources.quote_en: Pope Lucius III established the Inquisition at the Council of Verona in 1184, and its organization and procedures were perfected—if such a word can be used to describe that fearsome institution—by other popes.
38 The next step that the church took was to establish the Inquisition, a tribunal set up to suppress heresy.

events.title_en: Pope Innocent III condemns lay translation and discussion of the Bible
events.description_en: In 1199 Pope Innocent III wrote against "heretics" who translated the Bible into French and discussed it, applying Matthew 7:6 to them. His letter was later cited to justify banning the Bible's use and translation. The bishop of Metz had complained of such Bible reading, likely by the Waldenses.
events.description_ta: b 1199-⁠ம் வருடத்திலேயே, மக்கள் தங்கள் சொந்த மொழியில் பைபிளை வாசித்து அதைக் குறித்து கலந்து பேசுகிறார்கள் என்பதாக போப் மூன்றாம் இன்னசென்ட்டிடம் வடகிழக்கு பிரான்ஸிலுள்ள மெட்ஸின் பிஷப் முறையிட்டார்.

sources.title_en: They Tried to Keep God’s Word From the Masses
sources.quote_en: In 1199, Pope Innocent III wrote concerning “heretics” who had translated the Bible into French and dared to discuss it among themselves.
b As early as 1199, the bishop of Metz, in northeastern France, complained to Pope Innocent III that individuals were reading and discussing the Bible in the vernacular.

events.title_en: Albigensian Crusade against the Cathari of southern France
events.title_ta: அது அல்பிஜென்சியர்களின் சிலுவைப்போர் (1209-29) என அறியப்படலாயிற்று. d
events.description_en: Pope Innocent III ordered the Albigenses (Cathari) persecuted, and a crusade (1209-1229) followed, including the massacre of 20,000 at Béziers. Peace came in 1229 with the Albigenses defeated, and the Council of Narbonne forbade laymen to possess any part of the Bible.
events.description_ta: அது அல்பிஜென்சியர்களின் சிலுவைப்போர் (1209-29) என அறியப்படலாயிற்று. d

sources.title_en: The Troubadours—More Than Singers of Love Songs
sources.quote_en: It became known as the Albigensian Crusade (1209-29).d
37 A crusade was mounted against the “heretics,” and the Catholic crusaders massacred 20,000 men, women, and children in Béziers, France.
In 1229 the Catholic Church completed its Crusade against the Cathari, or Albigenses, in the south of France.c The Waldenses next became objects of such efforts.

events.title_en: Fourth Lateran Council anathematizes the Waldenses
events.title_ta: வால்டென்ஸ்களுக்கு எதிராக 1215-⁠ல் நான்காவது லேட்டரன் பொதுக் குழு போட்ட தடையால் சர்ச் கண்டனங்கள் உச்சக்கட்டத்தை எட்டின
events.description_en: Church condemnations that progressively drove the Waldenses into "heresy" culminated in the anathema issued against them by the Fourth Lateran Council in 1215.
events.description_ta: வால்டென்ஸ்களுக்கு எதிராக 1215-⁠ல் நான்காவது லேட்டரன் பொதுக் குழு போட்ட தடையால் சர்ச் கண்டனங்கள் உச்சக்கட்டத்தை எட்டின.

sources.quote_en: Church condemnations culminated in the anathema that the Fourth Lateran Council issued against the Waldenses in 1215.

events.title_en: Vaudès dies; Waldenses dispersed by persecution
events.description_en: Vaudès died in 1217, and persecution dispersed his followers into the French Alpine valleys, Germany, northern Italy, and Central and Eastern Europe.
events.description_ta: 1217-⁠ம் வருடம் வாடீ இறந்தார்; அவரைப் பின்பற்றியவர்கள், துன்புறுத்துதல் காரணமாக பிரான்ஸின் மலைப்பாங்கான பள்ளத்தாக்குகள், ஜெர்மனி, வட இத்தாலி, மத்திய மற்றும் கிழக்கு ஐரோப்பிய நாடுகள் என நாலாபுறமும் சிதறிப் போனார்கள்.

sources.quote_en: Vaudès died in the year 1217, and persecution dispersed his followers into the French Alpine valleys, Germany, northern Italy, and Central and Eastern Europe.

events.title_en: Council of Toulouse bans laymen from possessing vernacular Bibles
events.description_en: In 1229 the Council of Toulouse, aiming at the Albigenses and Waldenses, prohibited laymen from possessing the books of the Old or New Testament in the common language; only liturgical books in Latin were allowed.
events.description_ta: எந்த பைபிள் புத்தகத்தையும் யாரும் வைத்திருக்கக் கூடாது என்று டெளலோஸ் குழு தடை செய்ததன் மூலம் 1229-ல் இவர்களைக் கட்டுப்படுத்த முயன்றது.

sources.quote_en: The Council of Toulouse tried to check them in 1229 by banning the possession of Scriptural books.

Says the Enciclopedia Cattolica (Catholic Encyclopedia): “In 1229, the Council of Toulouse prohibited laymen from using them [vernacular Bibles] in view of the fight against the Albigenses and the Waldenses . . .

events.title_en: Waldenses stop preaching in public
events.description_en: Fearing the Inquisition, by 1230 the Waldenses no longer preached in public, devoting themselves instead to maintaining existing believers.
events.description_ta: 1230-⁠ல் அவர்கள் இனியும் வெளிப்படையாக பிரசங்கித்து வரவில்லை.

sources.quote_en: By 1230 they no longer preached in public. Audisio explains: “Rather than going to seek new sheep . . . , they devoted themselves to looking after the converted, maintaining them in their faith in the face of ...

events.title_en: Medieval Inquisition begins in Italy and France
events.description_en: The medieval Inquisition began in 1231 in Italy and France.
events.description_ta: இவை 1231-ல் இத்தாலியிலும் பிரான்ஸிலும் நிறுவப்பட்டன.

sources.quote_en: b Although their methods and results differed little, these two institutions were new with respect to the medieval Inquisition that had begun in 1231 in Italy and France.

events.title_en: Assembly at Tarragona under James I of Aragon bans vernacular Bibles
events.title_ta: 1234-ஆம் ஆண்டில் ஸ்பெயினிலுள்ள டாரகோனாவில் முதலாம் ஜேம்ஸின் தலைமையில் நடத்தப்பட்ட மாநாட்டில் இதேபோன்ற தடை விதிக்கப்பட்டது. . .
events.description_en: An assembly held at Tarragona, Spain, under James I of Aragon issued a prohibition similar to that of Toulouse against vernacular Bibles.
events.description_ta: 1234-ஆம் ஆண்டில் ஸ்பெயினிலுள்ள டாரகோனாவில் முதலாம் ஜேம்ஸின் தலைமையில் நடத்தப்பட்ட மாநாட்டில் இதேபோன்ற தடை விதிக்கப்பட்டது. . . .

events.title_en: Acre, last crusader stronghold, falls
events.title_ta: 1291-ல் சிலுவைப் போர் வீரர்களின் கடைசி அரணான பட்டணமாகிய ஏக்கர் முஸ்லிம்களிடம் வீழ்ச்சியடைந்தது
events.description_en: In 1291 Acre, the last crusader stronghold, fell to the Muslims, ending two centuries of Crusades in which political and economic interests dominated. The last major Crusade had begun in 1270.
events.description_ta: 1291-ல் சிலுவைப் போர் வீரர்களின் கடைசி அரணான பட்டணமாகிய ஏக்கர் முஸ்லிம்களிடம் வீழ்ச்சியடைந்தது.

sources.quote_en: In 1291 the city of Acre, the last crusader stronghold, fell to the Muslims.

events.title_en: Anne of Bohemia, reader of Wycliffe's Gospels, marries Richard II
events.title_ta: இவர் 1382-ல் இங்கிலாந்தின் எதிர்கால அரசர் இரண்டாம் ரிச்சர்டை திருமணம் செய்திருந்தார்
events.description_en: Anne of Bohemia, who studied Wycliffe's English Gospels, married King Richard II of England in 1382. She encouraged Prague students to study at Oxford, carrying Wycliffe's works back to Prague, which later supported Jan Hus.
events.description_ta: இவர் 1382-ல் இங்கிலாந்தின் எதிர்கால அரசர் இரண்டாம் ரிச்சர்டை திருமணம் செய்திருந்தார்.

events.title_en: Wycliffe's English Bible released
events.description_en: About 1382, shortly before Wycliffe died, his team released the first English version of the entire Bible, translated from the Latin Vulgate and copied by hand. His followers, the Lollards, circulated it throughout England; a revised, easier version followed about ten years later.

About 1382, John Wycliffe and his associates produced the first Bible translation in English.

sources.quote_en: Nearly two centuries earlier, about 1380, John Wycliffe had whetted the appetite of English-speaking people with a translation of the Bible from Latin.

events.description_en: Because of his prominence, Wycliffe was allowed to die in peace on the last day of 1384, though his Lollard followers were later persecuted.

sources.title_en: The Reformation—The Search Took a New Turn

events.title_en: Authorities order Jan Hus to stop preaching Wycliffe's ideas
events.description_en: In 1403 authorities ordered Jan Hus, rector of the University of Prague, to stop preaching Wycliffe's antipapal ideas, and Wycliffe's books were publicly burned.

sources.title_en: The Reformation—The Search Took a New Turn
sources.quote_en: In 1403 the authorities ordered him to stop preaching the antipapal ideas of Wycliffe, whose books they also publicly burned.

events.title_en: Jan Hus condemned and excommunicated
events.description_en: After writing stinging indictments of church practices, including the sale of indulgences, Hus was condemned and excommunicated in 1410.
events.description_ta: ஆனால் ஹஸ், ரோமன் சர்ச்சின் படுமோசமான சில பழக்கவழக்கங்களை கடுமையாக கண்டித்து தொடர்ந்து புத்தகங்கள் எழுதினார்; அதில் பாவ மன்னிப்புச் சீட்டுகள் விற்கப்படுவதை பெரிதும் கண்டித்தார்.a கடைசியாக, 1410-ல் குற்றவாளியென்று தீர்க்கப்பட்டு சர்ச்சிலிருந்தே விலக்கப்பட்டார்.

sources.title_en: The Reformation—The Search Took a New Turn
sources.quote_en: Hus, however, went on to write some of the most stinging indictments against the practices of the church, including the sale of indulgences.a He was condemned and excommunicated in 1410.

events.title_en: Archbishop Arundel denounces Wycliffe for translating the Scriptures
events.description_en: In a 1412 letter to Pope John XXIII, Archbishop Arundel called Wycliffe a "son of the old serpent," condemning him above all for devising "a new translation of the scriptures into the mother tongue."
events.description_ta: 1412-ல் போப் ஜான் XXIII-க்கு எழுதிய கடிதமொன்றில், பேராயர் அரண்டெல், இவரை “அந்த உதவாக்கரையான, எரிச்சலைமூட்டும் பயல் ஜான் வைக்கிளிப், நினைத்தாலே குமட்டிக்கொண்டு வரும் அந்த மனிதன், பழைய பாம்பின் மைந்தன், அந்திக்கிறிஸ்துவின் முன்னோடியும் பிள்ளையும்” என்பதாக குறிப்பிட்டிருந்தார்.

sources.title_en: Part Two—How the Bible Came to Us
sources.quote_en: In a letter to Pope John XXIII in 1412, Archbishop Arundel referred to “that wretched and pestilent fellow John Wycliffe, of damnable memory, that son of the old serpent, the very herald and child of antichrist.”

events.title_en: Hus summoned to the Council of Constance under false safe-conduct
events.description_en: Falsely promised safe-conduct, Hus was tricked into coming before the Council of Constance in 1414 to defend his views before 2,933 clergymen.

events.title_en: Jan Hus burned at the stake
events.description_en: Refusing to recant unless proved wrong from the Scriptures, Hus was condemned as a heretic by the Council of Constance and burned at the stake in 1415, praying aloud.

events.title_en: The Spanish Inquisition

events.description_en: By 1495 all or part of the Bible had been printed in German, Italian, French, Czech, Dutch, Hebrew, Catalan, Greek, Spanish, Slavonic, Portuguese, and Serbian, in that order.

events.title_en: Savonarola excommunicated
events.description_en: Dominican monk Girolamo Savonarola of Florence, who denounced corruption in Church and State, was excommunicated by the pope in 1497.
events.description_ta: 1497-ல் இவரை திருச்சபையிலிருந்து போப் விலக்கி வைத்தார்.

sources.title_en: The Reformation—The Search Took a New Turn

events.title_en: Savonarola arrested, tortured, and hanged

events.description_en: In 1498 Savonarola was arrested, tortured, and hanged; his body was burned and the ashes thrown into the Arno.

sources.title_en: The Reformation—The Search Took a New Turn
sources.quote_en: The following year, he was arrested, tortured, and hanged.

events.title_en: Luther enters University of Erfurt and first reads the Bible
events.description_en: In 1501 Martin Luther became a student at the University of Erfurt, where he read the Bible for the first time in its library.
events.description_ta: மார்ட்டின் 1501-⁠ல் எர்ஃபர்ட் பல்கலைக்கழகத்தில் மாணவராக சேர்ந்தார்.

sources.title_en: Martin Luther—The Man and His Legacy
sources.quote_en: In 1501, Martin became a student at the University of Erfurt.

events.title_en: Complutensian Polyglot — first printed Greek "New Testament"
events.description_en: The first printed edition of the Christian Greek Scriptures appeared in the Complutensian Polyglott (Greek and Latin) of 1514-1517.

sources.quote_en: The first printed edition of the Christian Greek Scriptures was that appearing in the Complutensian Polyglott (in Greek and Latin), of 1514-1517.

sources.quote_en: These were based mainly on Erasmus’ text, with corrections according to the Complutensian Polyglott of 1522 and 15 late cursive manuscripts of the previous few centuries.

events.title_en: Erasmus publishes first complete printed Greek text
events.description_en: In 1516 Dutch scholar Desiderius Erasmus published the first complete printed edition of the Greek text of the Christian Scriptures. It contained errors but was improved in four editions from 1519 to 1535 and became the basis for Luther's and Tyndale's translations.
events.description_ta: டச்சு கல்விமான் டெசிடீரியஸ் இராஸ்மஸ், 1516-ல் முழு கிரேக்க வாசகத்தின் முதல் அச்சுப் பதிப்பை உண்டுபண்ணினார்.

sources.title_en: Part Two—How the Bible Came to Us

sources.title_en: Part Two—How the Bible Came to Us
sources.quote_en: Erasmus’ Greek text 1516
Then in 1516 the Dutch scholar Desiderius Erasmus published his first edition of a master Greek text of the Christian Greek Scriptures.

sources.title_en: Study Number 6—The Christian Greek Text of the Holy Scriptures
sources.quote_en: It was during this early revival of learning that the famous Dutch scholar Desiderius Erasmus produced his first edition of a master Greek text of the “New Testament.”

events.title_en: Luther posts his 95 theses — start of the Protestant Reformation
events.title_ta: புராட்டஸ்டன்டு சீர்திருத்த இயக்கம் 1517-ம் ஆண்டு அக்டோபர் 31-ல் அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாக தொடங்கியதென்று சொல்லலாம்
events.description_en: Indignant at John Tetzel's sale of indulgences, Martin Luther, according to tradition, nailed 95 theses to the castle church door at Wittenberg on October 31, 1517. Printed and spread widely, they made church reform a Europe-wide controversy.
events.description_ta: புராட்டஸ்டன்டு சீர்திருத்த இயக்கம் 1517-ம் ஆண்டு அக்டோபர் 31-ல் அதிகாரப்பூர்வமாக தொடங்கியதென்று சொல்லலாம்.

sources.title_en: Martin Luther—The Man and His Legacy
sources.quote_en: In the autumn of 1517, he wrote his famous 95 theses, accusing the church of financial, doctrinal, and religious abuse.

sources.title_en: 500 Years of Calvinism—What Has It Achieved?
sources.quote_en: It is popularly thought that in 1517 he nailed his 95 theses, or protests, to a church door in Wittenberg, urging church reform.

events.title_en: Erasmus: "The shamelessness of the Roman Curia has reached its climax"
events.description_en: In 1518, amid papal corruption, Catholic scholar Erasmus wrote that the shamelessness of the Roman Curia had reached its climax.
events.description_ta: ஆக, “ரோம நிர்வாக குழுவின் வெட்கக்கேடான நிலை உச்சக்கட்டத்தை எட்டியது” என 1518-ல் டச்சு கத்தோலிக்க அறிஞர் ஈராஸ்மஸ் எழுதியது நூற்றுக்கு நூறு உண்மை.

sources.title_en: The Reformation—The Search Took a New Turn
sources.quote_en: It was with full justification that the Dutch Catholic scholar Erasmus wrote in 1518: “The shamelessness of the Roman Curia has reached its climax.”

events.title_en: Zwingli begins preaching reform in Zurich
events.description_en: Around 1519, Catholic priest Ulrich (Huldrych) Zwingli, then living in Zurich, began preaching against indulgences, Mariolatry, clerical celibacy, and other Catholic doctrines.
events.description_ta: சுமார் 1519-ல் பாவ மன்னிப்பு, மரியாள் வழிபாடு, குருமார் மணத்துறவு போன்ற இன்னும் பிற கத்தோலிக்க சர்ச்சின் கோட்பாடுகளையெல்லாம் தாக்கி ஸ்விங்லி பிரச்சாரம் செய்ய ஆரம்பித்தார்.

sources.title_en: The Reformation—The Search Took a New Turn
sources.quote_en: Around 1519, Zwingli began to preach against indulgences, Mariolatry, clerical celibacy, and other doctrines of the Catholic Church.

sources.title_en: Huldrych Zwingli’s Search for Bible Truth
sources.quote_en: By 1519, he was living in Zurich, the center of political influence in Switzerland.

events.title_en: Pope Leo X's bull against books containing "heresies"
events.description_en: On June 15, 1520, Pope Leo X issued a bull ordering that no book containing "heresies" be printed, sold, or read in any Catholic land.
events.description_ta: ஜூன் 15, 1520-ல், “முரண் சமய கருத்துக்கள்” அடங்கிய எந்தவொரு புத்தகத்தையும் எந்தக் கத்தோலிக்க நாடெங்கும் அச்சடிக்கவோ விற்கவோ வாசிக்கவோ கூடாது என்ற ஆணையைப் பத்தாம் போப் லியோ பிறப்பித்தார்; மேலும் உலக அதிகாரங்கள் அந்த ஆணையைத் தங்கள் ஆட்சி எல்லைகளில் அமல்படுத்துமாறு கோரினார்.

sources.title_en: A Printer Who Left His Mark
sources.quote_en: On June 15, 1520, Pope Leo X had issued a bull ordering that no book containing “heresies” be printed, sold, or read in any Catholic land and demanding that the secular authorities enforce the bull within their domains.

events.title_en: Papal bull against Luther; Luther burns it publicly
events.title_ta: லூத்தர் பிரச்சாரம் செய்யக்கூடாதென்றும், அவருடைய புத்தகங்களெல்லாம் எரிக்கப்பட வேண்டுமென்றும் 1520-ல் போப் ஓர் அரசாணை பிறப்பித்தார்
events.description_en: In 1520 the pope issued a bull forbidding Luther to preach and ordering his books burned; Luther defiantly burned the bull in public.
events.description_ta: லூத்தர் பிரச்சாரம் செய்யக்கூடாதென்றும், அவருடைய புத்தகங்களெல்லாம் எரிக்கப்பட வேண்டுமென்றும் 1520-ல் போப் ஓர் அரசாணை பிறப்பித்தார்.

sources.title_en: The Reformation—The Search Took a New Turn
sources.quote_en: In 1520 the pope issued a bull, or edict, that forbade Luther to preach and ordered that his books be burned.

sources.title_en: Martin Luther—The Man and His Legacy
sources.quote_en: Defiant, Luther publicly burned the papal bull containing the threat and published additional works that encouraged the principalities to reform the church even without the pope’s agreement.

events.title_en: Luther excommunicated; outlawed at the Diet of Worms
events.title_ta: 1521-⁠ல் பத்தாம் போப் லியோ, லூத்தரை சபை நீக்கம் செய்தார்
events.description_en: Pope Leo X excommunicated Luther in 1521. In April 1521 Luther appeared before Emperor Charles V at the Diet of Worms, refused to recant unless proved wrong from the Bible, and was declared an outlaw by the Edict of Worms.
events.description_ta: 1521-⁠ல் பத்தாம் போப் லியோ, லூத்தரை சபை நீக்கம் செய்தார்.

sources.title_en: Martin Luther—The Man and His Legacy
sources.quote_en: In 1521, Pope Leo X excommunicated Luther.

sources.title_en: The Reformation—The Search Took a New Turn
sources.quote_en: In defiance Luther burned the papal bull in public. The pope excommunicated him in 1521.

sources.title_en: They Tried to Keep God’s Word From the Masses
sources.quote_en: Martin Luther’s attempts to reform the Catholic Church and his eventual break with it in 1521 were based essentially on his understanding of Scripture.

events.title_en: Zwingli charged with heresy; resigns as Catholic priest
events.description_en: In 1522, after the clergy moved against practices contrary to church doctrine, Zwingli was charged with heresy and resigned from the Catholic priesthood.
events.description_ta: 1522-ல் குருமார்கள் சூரிச்சில் இருந்த அரசியல்வாதிகளை கைக்குள் போட்டுக்கொண்டு, சர்ச் போதனைகளுக்கு எதிராக மக்கள் நடக்காமல் பார்த்துக்கொண்டார்கள்.

sources.title_en: Huldrych Zwingli’s Search for Bible Truth
sources.quote_en: In 1522, the clergy tried to involve Zurich’s politicians in clamping down on practices that went against church doctrine.

events.title_en: Luther's German "New Testament" (September Bible) published
events.description_en: While hiding at Wartburg castle, Luther translated Erasmus' Greek text into German. Published in September 1522 without naming the translator, the "September Bible" was in staggering demand and was the first translation to use Erasmus' text.
events.description_ta: செப்டம்பர் 1522-⁠ல் பிரசுரிக்கப்பட்ட அது, செப்டம்பர் பைபிள் என அழைக்கப்பட்டது; மொழிபெயர்த்தவர் லூத்தர் என்று அதில் குறிப்பிடப்படவில்லை.

sources.title_en: Martin Luther—The Man and His Legacy
sources.quote_en: Published in September 1522 without identifying Luther as the translator, this work was known as the September Bible.

sources.title_en: Study Number 6—The Christian Greek Text of the Holy Scriptures
sources.quote_en: First to use Erasmus’ text was Martin Luther of Germany, who completed his translation of the Christian Greek Scriptures into German in 1522.

sources.title_en: Study Number 7—The Bible in Modern Times
sources.quote_en: Luther* 1522, 1534 M HErr Erasmus

events.title_en: Tyndale seeks Bishop Tunstall's support, then leaves England
events.title_ta: ஆகவே 1523-ல் டின்டேல், மொழிபெயர்ப்பு திட்டத்துக்கு அனுமதியும் ஆதரவும் திரட்டுவதற்கு லண்டனுக்கு பிஷப் டன்ஸ்டாலிடம் சென்றார்
events.description_en: Determined that even a plowboy should know the Scriptures, Tyndale went to London in 1523 to seek Bishop Tunstall's backing for a translation. Rebuffed, he left England, never to return.
events.description_ta: ஆகவே 1523-ல் டின்டேல், மொழிபெயர்ப்பு திட்டத்துக்கு அனுமதியும் ஆதரவும் திரட்டுவதற்கு லண்டனுக்கு பிஷப் டன்ஸ்டாலிடம் சென்றார்.

sources.title_en: Part Two—How the Bible Came to Us
sources.quote_en: So in 1523, Tyndale went to London to solicit the support of Bishop Tunstall for a translation project.

events.title_en: Tyndale begins translating from Hebrew and Greek in Germany
events.description_en: In 1524 Tyndale, having left England for Germany, began translating directly from the original Hebrew and Greek, later employing a press in Cologne.

sources.title_en: They Loved the Word of God
sources.quote_en: In 1524, Tyndale, having left England for Germany, began translating directly from the original Hebrew and Greek and then employed a press in Cologne to print copies.

events.title_en: Tyndale's "New Testament" completed; Cologne printing raided
events.description_en: Tyndale completed his English translation of the Christian Greek Scriptures from Erasmus' text by 1525, in exile. That year his printer in Cologne was raided, and Tyndale escaped up the Rhine with some of the pages.
events.description_ta: இந்த மொழிபெயர்ப்பாளர்தான் வில்லியம் டின்டேல்; 1525-ல் ஜெர்மனியிலுள்ள கொலோனில் தடைசெய்யப்பட்டிருந்த தன்னுடைய ஆங்கிலமொழி “புதிய ஏற்பாட்டை” அவர் பிரசுரிக்க முயற்சிசெய்துகொண்டிருந்தார்.

sources.title_en: Part One—How the Bible Came to Us
sources.quote_en: The translator in this case was William Tyndale, trying to produce his banned English “New Testament” at Cologne, Germany, in 1525.

sources.title_en: Study Number 6—The Christian Greek Text of the Holy Scriptures
sources.quote_en: In the face of much persecution, William Tyndale of England followed with his English translation from Erasmus’ text, completing this while in exile on the continent of Europe in 1525.

sources.title_en: The King James Version—How It Became Popular
sources.quote_en: It was translated from the original Greek into English by 1525.

events.title_en: Luther marries Katharina von Bora
events.title_ta: 1525-⁠ல் மார்ட்டின் லூத்தர், முன்னாள் கன்னியாஸ்திரீ காட்டாரினா ஃபான் போரா என்பவரை மணந்தார்
events.description_en: In 1525 Martin Luther married Katharina von Bora, a former nun.
events.description_ta: 1525-⁠ல் மார்ட்டின் லூத்தர், முன்னாள் கன்னியாஸ்திரீ காட்டாரினா ஃபான் போரா என்பவரை மணந்தார்.

events.title_en: Tyndale's English "New Testament" printed at Worms reaches England
events.description_en: At least 3,000 copies of Tyndale's English "New Testament" were printed at Worms and began to be distributed in England early in 1526. Authorities burned copies publicly; Bishop Tunstall's purchases for burning unknowingly financed further editions.
events.description_ta: இவை இங்கிலாந்துக்கு அனுப்பி வைக்கப்பட்டு 1526 ஆரம்பத்தில் அங்கே விநியோகிக்கப்பட்டன.

sources.quote_en: These were sent to England and began to be distributed there early in 1526.

sources.quote_en: William Tyndale, who had to flee from England, produced his New Testament in 1526.

events.title_en: Robert Estienne takes over his father's Paris press
events.description_en: In 1526 Robert Estienne, a scholar of Latin, Greek, and Hebrew, took over his father Henri's press in Paris; Bible editions became a major focus of his work.
events.description_ta: 1526-ல் ஆன்ரீயின் அச்சகத்தை எடுத்து நடத்தியபோது, ராபெர் ஏட்டியென் ஏற்கெனவே உயர்ந்த மொழித் தராதரங்களில் நிபுணராக அறியப்பட்டிருந்தார்.

sources.title_en: A Printer Who Left His Mark
sources.quote_en: When he took over Henri’s press in 1526, Robert Estienne was already known as a scholar of high linguistic standards.

events.title_en: Miles Coverdale preaches against Catholic practices and flees England
events.description_en: By 1528 Coverdale was preaching against image worship, confession, and the Mass; his life in danger, he left England for the Continent for about seven years.

sources.title_en: Coverdale and the First Complete Printed English Bible
sources.quote_en: By 1528, Coverdale had started to preach in church against the unscriptural Catholic practices of image worship, confession, and the Mass.

events.title_en: German princes protest — origin of the name "Protestant"
events.description_en: In 1526 the emperor let each German state choose Lutheran or Catholic religion, but in 1529 he reversed the decision; some princes protested, and the name Protestant was coined.
events.description_ta: ஆனால் 1529-ல் இந்தத் தீர்மானத்தை பேரரசர் மாற்றியபோது ஜெர்மானிய பிரபுக்கள் சிலர் அதற்கு எதிர்ப்பு தெரிவித்தனர் (புரட்டஸ்ட் செய்தனர்); ஆகவே, இந்தச் சீர்திருத்த இயக்கத்திற்கு புராட்டஸ்டன்டு என்ற பெயர் சூட்டப்பட்டது.

sources.title_en: The Reformation—The Search Took a New Turn
sources.quote_en: 25 In the years following the Diet of Worms, the Reformation movement gained so much popular support that in 1526 the emperor granted each German state the right to choose its own form of religion, Lutheran or Roman ...

events.title_en: Tyndale's Pentateuch — first English translation from Hebrew; uses "Jehovah"
events.title_ta: 1530-ல், டின்டேல் எபிரெய வேதாகமத்தின் முதல் ஐந்து புத்தகங்களாகிய ஐந்தாகமத்தின் (Pentateuch) பதிப்பை வெளியிட்டார்
events.description_en: In 1530 Tyndale produced an edition of the Pentateuch, becoming the first to translate from Hebrew directly into English and the first English translator to use the name Jehovah.
events.description_ta: 1530-ல், டின்டேல் எபிரெய வேதாகமத்தின் முதல் ஐந்து புத்தகங்களாகிய ஐந்தாகமத்தின் (Pentateuch) பதிப்பை வெளியிட்டார்.

sources.title_en: Part Two—How the Bible Came to Us
sources.quote_en: In 1530, Tyndale produced an edition of the Pentateuch, the first five books of the Hebrew Scriptures.

sources.title_en: How the Bible Came to Us
sources.quote_en: For example, in 1530, Englishman William Tyndale, educated at Oxford, produced an edition of the Pentateuch, the first five books of the Hebrew Scriptures.

events.title_en: Antonio Brucioli's Italian translation from Erasmus' text
events.title_ta: இத்தாலியின் அன்சோனியோ புரூசியோலி, 1530-ல் இராஸ்மஸின் வாக்கியத்தை இத்தாலிய மொழியில் மொழிபெயர்த்தார்
events.description_en: Antonio Brucioli of Italy translated Erasmus' Greek text into Italian in 1530.
events.description_ta: இத்தாலியின் அன்சோனியோ புரூசியோலி, 1530-ல் இராஸ்மஸின் வாக்கியத்தை இத்தாலிய மொழியில் மொழிபெயர்த்தார்.

sources.title_en: Study Number 6—The Christian Greek Text of the Holy Scriptures
sources.quote_en: Antonio Brucioli of Italy translated Erasmus’ text into Italian in 1530.

events.title_en: Augsburg Confession rejected; Protestant-Catholic rift irreconcilable
events.title_ta: அடுத்த வருடம் 1530-ல், ஆக்ஸ்பர்க் கூட்டத்தில் இரு தரப்பினருக்கும் இடையே சமரசம் செய்து வைக்க பேரரசர் முயற்சிகளை மேற்கொண்டார்
events.description_en: At the Diet of Augsburg in 1530, the Lutherans presented the Augsburg Confession composed by Melanchthon; its rejection by Rome made the rift between Protestantism and Catholicism irreconcilable.
events.description_ta: அடுத்த வருடம் 1530-ல், ஆக்ஸ்பர்க் கூட்டத்தில் இரு தரப்பினருக்கும் இடையே சமரசம் செய்து வைக்க பேரரசர் முயற்சிகளை மேற்கொண்டார்.

sources.title_en: The Reformation—The Search Took a New Turn
sources.quote_en: The next year, 1530, at the Diet of Augsburg, an effort was made by the emperor to mend the differences between the two parties.

events.title_en: Zurich Bible (German) produced by Zwingli's group
events.title_ta: 1520-ல் சில நிபுணர்களின் ஒரு தொகுதியோடு சேர்ந்து அவர் வேலை செய்தார்
events.description_en: During the 1520s Zwingli led scholars translating from Hebrew and Greek; the resulting Zurich Bible (Zürcher) is dated 1531.
events.description_ta: 1520-ல் சில நிபுணர்களின் ஒரு தொகுதியோடு சேர்ந்து அவர் வேலை செய்தார்.

sources.title_en: Huldrych Zwingli’s Search for Bible Truth
sources.quote_en: Zwingli’s most meaningful work was the translation of the Bible.
